blocks.text: Most internal auditors spend part of every day in email. You request evidence, chase control owners, forward policies and keep a trail of who said what. Outlook carries much of that work. The Mac app changed a lot in 2026, so old habits may not match the menus you see now. This guide covers the parts that matter for audit work, with the menu paths and shortcuts to check.
Why audit email needs its own Outlook setup

Email volume is high for everyone, not only auditors. Microsoft's Work Trend Index says the average worker receives 117 emails a day, and most are skimmed in under 60 seconds. The same report counts 275 interruptions a day from meetings, emails and chats. Those figures come from Microsoft 365 telemetry across all workers, through February 15, 2025. They are not audit-specific, so read them as a rough picture. They still show why a clean setup pays off.
What changed in Outlook for Mac in 2026

Microsoft now centers its Mac email on the new Outlook for Mac. The release notes show a steady run of changes this year. Check them against your own build, because menus differ between versions. These are the changes that matter most for audit work.

items: Version 16.108, April 14, 2026: opens and imports .msg files, which helps when a single message arrives as a file.
April 14, 2026: Settings were completely redesigned, so look for options in new places.
Version 16.110, June 16, 2026: Import PST brings in emails, calendars, contacts and other mailbox data.
July 14, 2026: you can customize the left navigation rail.
September 16, 2026: right-click Mail, Calendar or People in the rail to open it in a separate window.
Version 16.114.3, build 26102720, October 27, 2026: quality and performance improvements only.

blocks.text: The PST import matters most if you inherited an old audit archive. Check your version first, then look for Import PST in the app. Import from a copy of the PST file, not the original, so the source stays untouched. Read each prompt before you confirm, because the release notes do not describe every option on the import screen.
The release notes page cut off during this check, so a newer build may already exist after 16.114.3. Look at the release notes yourself before you plan a rollout.
Legacy Outlook ends in October 2026: what to do now

Microsoft says support for legacy Outlook for Mac will end in October 2026. Whether you keep support depends on your Microsoft 365, Office or Outlook license. If your team still runs the legacy app, plan the move now. A rushed switch at the end of the month is the wrong time to find missing accounts.

Accounts do not carry over on their own. An account you add in the new Outlook for Mac does not automatically appear in Legacy Outlook, and the reverse is true too. During the switch, you may need to add each mailbox in both apps. Count your accounts before you start, including the shared mailboxes your team uses.

blocks.title: Count before you switch
blocks.text: Write down every account, shared mailbox and calendar you use. Then confirm each one appears in the app you plan to keep before you remove anything from the old app.

Microsoft's support page says you can go back with Help > Revert to Legacy Outlook. A Microsoft Q&A reply, which this guide could not confirm, says that option was removed in a later build. Open the Help menu and look for the option. If it is missing, do not count on switching back. Plan as if the move is one-way until you confirm otherwise.
Templates for repeat audit requests

Audit work repeats itself. You send the same evidence request to many owners, then the same follow-up a week later. A saved template keeps the wording consistent and saves typing. Built-in templates work for Microsoft 365 subscribers and for Outlook for Mac 15.35 (170610) and later. Here is the process.

items: Open a new message and write the request once. Use brackets such as [Owner], [Control] and [Due date] for the parts that change.
Choose File > Save As Template.
To reuse it later, choose File > New > Mail From Template.
Outlook opens the template as an .emltpl file. Fill in the brackets, check the recipients and send.

blocks.text: Clean the message before you save it. Remove the reply chain, the old signature block and any real client names. A template that still carries last quarter's thread can leak into the next email. This is an easy mistake to make, and it is hard to notice after you send.

Worked example. Your request reads: 'Please send [document] for [control] by [due date]. The sample period is [period].' You save it once. At the next audit, you open the template, fill in the brackets and send it. The wording stays the same, and every owner gets the same clear request.
Shared audit mailboxes and My Templates

Many audit teams share a mailbox for requests and replies. Templates get tricky there. Microsoft says the My Templates add-in is available for Exchange accounts, but it is not available in shared mailboxes opened in Outlook for Mac. If your team works from a shared inbox, do not count on My Templates in that inbox.

Test built-in templates in the shared mailbox before you rely on them. Send one test message to yourself, open it and check the wording, signature and attachments. Then decide where the master copy lives. One option is to keep the master in your own account and paste the text into the shared mailbox when you need it. Another is to keep one copy in each place and update both when the wording changes.
If your team still needs to connect the mailbox, see [How to add a shared mailbox in Outlook on Mac](/how-to/add-a-shared-mailbox-in-outlook).
Search filters and finding the evidence email

Finding one email from months ago is a daily task for many auditors. Microsoft lists improved search in Outlook for Mac, opened with Shift+Command+F. Start with the sender's name and one word from the subject. Then check the results for the right thread, not only the newest message.

Worked example. The external auditor sent a sample list in March. Search for their name and the word 'sample'. Open the newest message, then the one before it, so you read the request and the reply in order. Note the date of each message in your working papers.
When you cannot find the search bar, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where it is. Lazur draws a circle and a label around the field on your screen.
Rules and what to check before you trust them

Rules help when a steady flow of evidence should land in one folder. Check what your account supports first. A Windows-focused report on new Outlook says server-side rules cannot play sounds, show desktop alerts, print, run scripts or move messages to a PST file. It also says IMAP and POP3 accounts have no rules. This guide could not confirm how Outlook for Mac handles each case, so test on your own account.

A short test settles it. Create a rule that moves one test message to a folder. Send that message to yourself and check the folder. Only then trust the rule with audit mail. If nothing moves, check the account type before you change the rule.

The step-by-step setup is in [How to create a rule in Outlook on Mac](/how-to/create-a-rule-in-outlook). Avoid one common trap: a rule that moves mail out of the inbox before you read it. A missed deadline can start that way.
Daily habits that cut inbox noise

Subject lines do most of the work. Microsoft's report says most emails are skimmed in under 60 seconds. Put the ask and the date in the subject. 'Evidence needed for access review, due Friday' gets read fast. 'Quick question' is easy to skip.

Open My Day to see what needs you today. Press Shift+Command+] to open it. Microsoft also lists snooze and suggested meeting times on its Outlook for Mac page, so you can push a message to later without losing it. The table below lists the shortcuts and paths from this guide.

blocks.text: Where Lazur helps during audit email

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Outlook or any other app. It works across apps, so the same question works in Excel or Word too.

Lazur explains and points. Ask what a thread says about a deadline, and Lazur reads what is on screen and answers. Ask where a control sits, and Lazur circles it. When you ask how to do something, Lazur guides you one click at a time and waits for each click.

Lazur drafts and dictates. Ask for a short follow-up, and Lazur drafts the text. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots help with the phrases you type every week.

Lazur also handles everyday tasks by voice. It can set Apple Reminders and Calendar events, open apps and links, and run web search. It does not click buttons, edit files or operate Outlook for you. You still read the draft and send the email.
Privacy and client evidence

Audit evidence is often sensitive, so ask how any assistant handles it. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

That does not replace your firm's rules. Check the policy on AI tools before you point any assistant at client records. If the policy says no, keep Lazur off that screen. You can still use the Outlook steps in this guide.
Mistakes people make with Outlook on Mac for audit work

items: Expecting My Templates in a shared mailbox. Microsoft says it is not available there in Outlook for Mac.
Assuming accounts move from the new app to Legacy Outlook. They do not move on their own.
Saving a template with a client name or an old reply chain still inside it.
Trusting a rule before a test message lands in the right folder. A Windows report says IMAP and POP3 accounts have no rules.
Waiting until October 2026 to plan the switch away from legacy Outlook.

blocks.text: Next steps for this week

items: Find your Outlook for Mac build number and compare it with the release notes.
List every account and shared mailbox your team uses. Check which app each one lives in.
Save one template, send a test to yourself and check the wording and brackets.
Test one rule with one message before you rely on it.
Ask Lazur to point at the search bar and walk you through the template menu, one click at a time.

faq.question: Is the new Outlook for Mac the same as Legacy Outlook?
faq.answer: No. Microsoft says accounts added in the new Outlook for Mac do not automatically carry over to Legacy Outlook, and the reverse is also true. Microsoft also says support for legacy Outlook for Mac ends in October 2026.

faq.question: Do I need Microsoft 365 to use templates in Outlook for Mac?
faq.answer: Microsoft lists built-in template controls as available to Microsoft 365 subscribers and to Outlook for Mac 15.35 (170610) and later. If you are not sure which applies to you, check your license and your build number.

faq.question: Why does My Templates not show up in our shared mailbox?
faq.answer: Microsoft says My Templates is available for Exchange accounts but is not available in shared mailboxes opened in Outlook for Mac. Test built-in templates in the shared mailbox before you rely on them.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons or send email for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points, explains, guides, drafts and dictates. When you ask for steps, it guides you one click at a time and waits for each click. You click, and you send.

faq.question: Is Lazur an add-in for Outlook?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. It is not a plugin or add-in for any app, and it has no partnerships with any app maker.

faq.question: Does Lazur store my audit emails or screenshots?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Check your firm's AI policy before you use it on client records.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.

faq.question: What is the latest Outlook for Mac version this guide can confirm?
faq.answer: The release notes page checked for this guide lists version 16.114.3, build 26102720, dated October 27, 2026. The page cut off during the check, so a newer build may already exist.
